hold_text: Dispatched to this lane as Tier-1 (PI-20260927-YZRZQ725-0004 / review-pack item D4: 'add a Tier-1 checklist row: extend scripts/analysis/classify_paper_records.py with a pairs-strategy-aware bucket'), on the premise that scripts/analysis/** and tests/** are Tier-1 surface. Read scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py IN FULL as instructed and verified that premise MECHANICALLY, not assumed: TIER1_SURFACE (the file's own allowlist) does not list scripts/analysis/** or src/analysis/** anywhere -- grep for 'analysis' in that file returns zero hits. The fix's correct home is src/analysis/paper_record_classifier.py::classify_record (that is where every other bucket -- A/B/C -- is already defined; scripts/analysis/classify_paper_records.py is the thin CLI wrapper around it), so the diff necessarily touches src/**, which TIER2_PATHS names explicitly (`"src/**"`). Ran `_match()` from the guard itself against the two changed non-test files to confirm rather than infer: src/analysis/paper_record_classifier.py -> TIER2_PATHS match True; scripts/analysis/classify_paper_records.py -> not in TIER1_SURFACE, not in TIER2_PATHS/TIER3_PATHS by name (an 'unvouched' path). Per R5's own logic this bars `landing: "self"` at tier 1 outright (`barred2` alone fails it, independent of TIER1_SURFACE coverage), so a false tier:1 self-land declaration would simply fail this same guard's own CI check rather than land anything -- filing it honestly here instead. Per docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md's Permission Tiers table this change IS Tier-1 in substance (a pure, stdlib-only, offline analysis/classification module -- no DB write, no order path, no runtime/deploy/service/timer touched, nothing that changes what trades); the mismatch is between that prose definition and this guard's mechanical TIER1_SURFACE allowlist, which has no carve-out for offline analysis code living under src/. Not resolved here: fixing check_pr_landing.py's own allowlist is itself LANDING_MACHINERY (R12) and may not self-land, so it needs its own separately-approved PR rather than being folded into this one. Requesting: an operator (or a Tier-2 approval-record) read of this diff and its evidence, and either (a) an explicit merge, or (b) a decision-round-trip / recorded approval this branch could satisfy under R15's scope_paths (src/analysis/paper_record_classifier.py, scripts/analysis/classify_paper_records.py, tests/test_paper_record_classifier.py, tests/fixtures/perf_review_20260924_20260927_window.json), or (c) a follow-up checklist row to widen TIER1_SURFACE to cover src/analysis/** and scripts/analysis/** generally (a genuine gap, separately filed) so a future PR like this one can self-land honestly.
why: Adds bucket P (pairs-strategy bilateral management exit) to src/analysis/paper_record_classifier.py::classify_record, matched structurally on strategy_name.startswith('pairs_') AND exit_reason.startswith('pairs_') on a status=='closed' row -- verified against src/units/strategies/pairs_engine.py::exit_signal (the only writer of the 'outcome' string: revert/stop/timeout) and pairs_executor.py::_close_pair, which both write exit_reason=f'pairs_{outcome}' (plus the half-open-cleanup path, outcome='half_open_cleanup'); journal strategy_name for a pairs leg is f'{pair_config_name}_a'/'_b' (_leg_strats), and every configured pair name in config/pairs.yaml already starts with 'pairs_'. MEASURED POPULATION: 52 real closed-paper-account rows pulled 2026-09-27 via `scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh 'journal?table=trades&limit=700'` (direct HTTPS GET, live ict-bot-arm VM, trade_journal.db), filtered to is_backtest!=1 AND account_class=='paper'-or-is_demo AND status=='closed' AND closed_at in [2026-09-24T16:00Z, 2026-09-27T07:29:44Z] (the performance-review PR #13085 window) -- committed verbatim (trimmed to classifier-read fields only) at tests/fixtures/perf_review_20260924_20260927_window.json. BEFORE the fix, run on this exact 52-row population: by_bucket = {A:12, B:1, C:39}; every one of the 26 pairs_sol_eth_*/pairs_bnb_btc_* rows fell to the generic 'unknown_exit:pairs_*' fallback (bucket C, because this DB-native row shape carries the executor's own backstop SL/TP levels, which _has_bracket() accepts as a real bracket) rather than the 'unclassified' fallback (bucket B) the review pack described -- a real, verified discrepancy from the bug report's premise (which likely ran against API-shaped rows lacking stop_loss/take_profit_1, per this module's own _normalize_api_row caveat: 'bucket-C bracket-based reconstruction eligibility is degraded for rows normalized this way'), but the same underlying miscategorization either way: a deliberate, correct pairs-executor close being read as either a technical artifact (B) or a broker-truncation needing reconstruction (C), neither of which it is. AFTER the fix, same 52 rows: by_bucket = {A:12, B:1, C:14, P:25} -- 25 of 26 pairs-strategy rows reclassify into the new bucket P; the 26th (journal id 6157, pairs_sol_eth_b, exit_reason=reconciler_filled -- a genuine broker/reconciler-forced close, not the executor's own decision) correctly stays in bucket C, unaffected, a positive control the test asserts explicitly. Also asserts (positive controls, unaffected by this change): a pairs leg's own decision/plumbing refusal stays bucket B, and a genuine non-pairs artifact (credential refusal) stays bucket B. Verified failing without the fix: temporarily `git stash`'d the two source files, re-ran the full test file -- 4 of 18 tests failed with the expected AssertionErrors (bucket C or 0-count where P/25 was expected), 14 unaffected pre-existing tests still passed; popped the stash and all 18 passed again. Files changed: src/analysis/paper_record_classifier.py (new bucket P + its match logic + updated docstring/precedence comment), scripts/analysis/classify_paper_records.py (surfaces the P count in the --format md report), tests/test_paper_record_classifier.py (7 new tests: bucket-P recognition on bracket/no-bracket/timeout/half-open-cleanup rows, 3 positive controls, the fixture-driven 52-row population test, and one existing test's by_bucket/by_strategy dict literals updated to include the new P:0 key), tests/fixtures/perf_review_20260924_20260927_window.json (new, the 52-row real population, provenance stated in the test file's docstring).
